note: As far outside the stated ICP as anyone in the corpus. He is a state-paid carer for his mother with two unlaunched side businesses and describes himself as 'a starving businessman'; income is about $2,500 a month with roughly $300 left at month end and $300 of available credit. Health is not a neglected corner of an otherwise good life — ankylosing spondylitis, an untreated hernia, two shoulder surgeries, raised lipids and schizoaffective disorder are the life. This is rescue in the most literal sense: he was in the process of applying for disability and is training to avoid it. He clears the exclusion criterion on the version that matters, since he is the opposite of gym-averse — an ex-wrestler who took himself from 265 lb to 223 lb with no programme at all — although he was more than 50 lb above his own target a year ago. Two observations for the ICP work. First, this is the sharpest evidence yet that the criteria have no clinical dimension: he is the prospect a clinical screen exists for, and none of the five criteria would have caught him. Second, he is simultaneously the worst commercial fit and the best product fit in the batch — he rated the offer a 10, named accountability and community as the thing he needed most, and has no family, no accountability and no community at all. An income screen alone reads that as a disqualification and says nothing about the fact that the funnel is delivering people in acute need to a $6,000 price point.
